newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares continuing breaking records.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares continuing breaking records.

text.p: Danish share prices, boosted by cleaning group ISS, forged ahead to a new closing high on Monday, the eighth new record in 11 trading days.

Dealers said there was scope for further gains on Tuesday but that the market could lack direction, with Wall Street closed for the President's Day holiday on Monday and therefore no Dow to show the way on Tuesday morning.
They added that players might also choose to stay on the sidelines until Denmark's two biggest banks published annual reports on Wednesday and Thursday.
"We could rise a quarter or a half percent tomorrow. There's a good floor in the market and the dollar is up," a trader said.
The KFX top-20 index closed 0.33 point up at 156.00, in overall bourse turnover of 1.2 billion crowns.
The KFX March future rose 0.20 point to 155.60, with 408 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.

Highest riser of the day was cleaning group ISS which jumped eight crowns, 4.2 percent, to 197 crowns on management forecasts of improved operating profits in 1996 and on continuing positive sentiment after the sale of its troubled U.S. subsidiary.

BG Bank, due to publish its annual report on February 24, rose nine crowns to 296, but Unidanmark and Den Danske Bank, reporting respectively on Wednesday and Thursday fared less well. Unidanmark fell three crowns to 347, while Den Danske edged up a single crown to 565.
